author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Al Jazeera has learned that Oman has sent a proposal to Iran on jointly managing the Strait of Hormuz, the crucial waterway that has effectively been closed since the start of the war between the US and Iran. 
Sources say Oman's joint mechanism would see countries pay a voluntary toll to pass the strait, while Tehran has demanded a mandatory fee and that ships use pre-approved routes. The closure has had a huge impact on crucial exports from the Gulf, including oil, gas, and fertilisers, with QatarEnergy warning a major European buyer that it will not be able to deliver LNG until late September, while Asian buyers face delays that could last into October. Before the war, around a fifth of the world's LNG and a quarter of the world's crude oil flowed through the strait, now down to a trickle. title: Strait of Hormuz crisis: Oman proposes deal with Iran as Qatar warns of LNG delays

description:
Three years of fighting between the army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces have devastated Sudan.
The conflict has caused the world's largest humanitarian crisis, displacing more than 13 million people and killing tens of thousands of civilians.
More than half of the population needs aid.
The health system is in ruins, and millions of children are out of school.
Both sides have been accused of war crimes and other abuses.
Recent fighting has centred around the city of el-Obeid, under siege by paramilitaries. 
The army has retaken a main highway linking it to the capital, which could weaken the RSF.
But hundreds of thousands of people trapped there are still at risk. 
So, what will it take to stop the conflict?

Presenter: James Bays

Guests:

description:
Keiko Fujimori has been sworn in as Peru's first female president, marking a historic moment in the country's political history and a return to the presidential palace 26 years after her father, former President Alberto Fujimori.

Her narrow election victory reflects a deeply divided nation. Supporters credit the Fujimori era with restoring economic stability and improving security, while critics continue to demand accountability for alleged human rights abuses committed during her father's presidency.

As she begins her term, Keiko Fujimori faces major challenges, including political polarisation, economic uncertainty, public expectations on crime and inflation, and the environmental impact of the El Niño phenomenon on Peru's fishing industry.

This report examines the challenges facing US-Iran diplomacy, the role of regional mediators, and what could happen next in one of the world's most dangerous geopolitical crises.
